root_motivation: Grounding: a 2026-09-29 explore run (dream-seeds-0929.txt §A) found 5 of 168 synthetic sessions calling host.quickstart with kind "event" or "webhook" and being refused UnknownKind (registered kinds: chain, echo, http, python, wasm; no data.docs/hint field) even though the capability they wanted -- the webhook-inbox recipe (http kind + host.trigger.*) -- has been live since PRD-mcphost-inbound-events/PRD-mcphost-webhook-inbox. An agent builder names the job ("webhook"), not mcphost's runtime taxonomy, so every such refusal is a lost first minute against a capability that already ships. This PRD adds a kind-alias table that routes those job-words to the existing recipe instead of refusing them, and gives a genuinely unknown kind the same data.docs/registered/did_you_mean shape PRD-mcphost-auth-error-names-argument already gave auth errors.
user_persona: The agent builder (persona or human) who knows "webhook"/"event"/"cron" but not mcphost's runtime kind names, and wants host.quickstart/host.tool_publish to route them to the working recipe instead of refusing; the explore/synthorg operator whose dx-findings should stop recording UnknownKind for these job-words; and the PM (Joe), for whom the webhook-inbox killer-app recipe should be reachable by its own name.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given host.quickstart called with kind: "webhook", When the server responds, Then the spec's kind is http, resolved_from is webhook, and recipe.steps lists host.tool_publish, host.trigger.set, host.trigger.test in order with args_example on each.
Given the same call with kind: "EVENT", When the server responds, Then it resolves identically (case-insensitive).

Given host.tool_publish with a valid http spec body but kind: "event", When the server responds, Then the tool is created with runtime kind http, the descriptor carries resolved_from: "event", and host.tool_call on it succeeds.

Given host.tool_publish with kind: "lambda", When the server responds, Then the JSON-RPC code is -32602, data.error_code is unknown_kind, data.registered lists the five kinds, data.aliases lists the aliases, data.did_you_mean contains python, and data.docs is host.quickstart.
Given the alias table, When the kindroute startup test runs, Then every alias resolves to a kind in the registered list and every recipe.steps[].tool is a registered tool.
Given contracts/host-tools.v1.json and www/llms.txt at the landing commit, When grepped, Then the kind description and the kinds paragraph both contain webhook and alias.
Given host.quickstart with no kind, When the server responds, Then the response lists kinds, aliases and recipes arrays.
Given cargo test at the landing commit, When it runs, Then every test that passed at v0.61.0 still passes and the kindroute_* tests for AC 1-7 pass, with the gate receipt showing block=0.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/kindroute_ac08_full_suite_green_at_landing.rs -- pins docs/benchmarks/kindroute-suite-gate.txt (1426 passed, 0 failed, 8 pre-existing ignored; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings: 0 warnings).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given prod after deploy-on-land, When a one-shot client sends host.quickstart with kind: "webhook" to https://mcphost.dev as a fresh synthetic tenant, Then the response has resolved_from: "webhook" and three recipe steps, and the following nightly explore's dx-findings.jsonl has zero unknown_kind rows for event/webhook (Live; evidence: the probe response and the dx-findings grep count, pasted into the receipt by the operator).

scope: src/kinds/aliases.rs (new): the KIND_ALIASES const table (alias/kind/recipe rows), find_alias (case-insensitive lookup), alias_names, recipe_names, recipe_steps -- the one data-driven place requirement 1 asks for.

src/control.rs: resolve_kind (shared by quickstart and tool_publish) resolves an exact registered kind name first, then the alias table; quickstart's response gains resolved_from/recipe when an alias fired, plus unconditional kinds/aliases/recipes arrays (AC7); tool_publish resolves before every downstream check (kind_mismatch, network/deps gates, storage) and its response gains resolved_from.

src/errors.rs: AppError::UnknownKind gains an aliases field; into_error_data adds data.registered/data.aliases/data.did_you_mean (curated FaaS-vocabulary hints plus a Levenshtein edit-distance pass over registered kinds + aliases, capped at 3); data.docs (host.quickstart) was already unconditional.

src/handler.rs: host.tool_publish's and host.quickstart's kind property descriptions now name the aliases; host.spec_test's UnknownKind construction updated for the new field (no alias resolution added there -- out of this PRD's requirement 2/3 scope).
contracts/host-tools.v1.json: regenerated via `mcphost contract dump` after the description-text edit above.
www/llms.txt: the "Publish a tool" paragraph (step 4) gains one sentence naming the aliases and the two recipes.
non_goals: New runtime kinds -- PRD's own non-goal; every alias resolves to the existing http kind, never a new Kind impl.
Changing trigger signature semantics -- PRD-mcphost-event-trigger-self-test's territory, untouched here.
Rewriting llms.txt beyond the kinds paragraph.

Requirement 7 (unknown_kind_total{requested} metrics counter) and requirement 8 (registry listing advertises "receive webhooks") -- P1/P2 requirements with no corresponding AC in the coder dispatch's list; not attempted this tick.

additional.did_you_mean_is_not_pure_edit_distance: Requirement 4 describes did_you_mean as 'edit distance ≤ 2 against kinds and aliases, max 3', but AC4's own example (kind: "lambda" must suggest python) has a Levenshtein distance of 6 from every registered kind/alias -- no threshold-≤2 pass produces it. Resolved by adding a small curated synonym table (DID_YOU_MEAN_HINTS in errors.rs: lambda/function/functions/serverless/faas → python) checked before the edit-distance pass, which stays the mechanism for an actual typo ("pythom", "htpp"). The AC (what tests must prove) wins over the requirement prose's algorithm description where the two conflict.

five_whys_trace.q: Why route job-words to a recipe instead of just improving the UnknownKind error message?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal 1 (PRD TL;DR): the capability the agent wants (webhook-inbox) already exists and is measured nightly -- a better error message still ends in a refusal; routing kind="webhook" straight to a working http spec plus the host.trigger.set/test steps turns the first call into a success instead of a well-explained failure.

five_whys_trace.q: Why resolve aliases in one shared function (control::resolve_kind) rather than duplicating the lookup in quickstart and tool_publish?
five_whys_trace.a: Both call sites need the identical registered-name-wins-then-alias-table behavior and must fail with the identical UnknownKind data payload -- a second, hand-copied version of that logic is exactly the kind of drift PRD-mcphost-tenant-key-missing-is-invalid-params's field_and_expected/docs helpers were already built to avoid for error shaping.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.tool_publish resolve kind_name to the runtime kind BEFORE the kind_mismatch/network/deps checks, rather than leaving kind_name as the alias string and only translating it at storage time?
five_whys_trace.a: Those checks (infer_kind_signal's http/python mismatch check, the python-only network/deps gates) match on kind_name.as_str() directly -- leaving it as "event" would silently skip kind_mismatch detection for an alias'd http publish and misclassify it against the python-only gates; resolving first means every downstream check runs against the kind that will actually be stored.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC7's kinds/aliases/recipes addition apply unconditionally rather than only when kind is omitted?
five_whys_trace.a: The AC's Given is 'host.quickstart with no kind', but gating the fields on that condition would mean a caller who already knows one kind can't discover the others without a second, kind-less call -- additive fields cost nothing for the existing tests (verified: no test asserts an exact/closed key set on quickstart's response) and are strictly more useful shipped on every response.

ambiguities_resolved.question: did_you_mean's algorithm: strict edit-distance-≤2 threshold (as requirement 4's prose reads literally) or something looser?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: AC4 is the hard contract and cannot be satisfied by a strict ≤2 threshold (lambda→python is edit distance 6). Resolved with a curated synonym hint table checked first (lambda/function/functions/serverless/faas → python), falling back to the edit-distance-≤2 pass requirement 4 describes for genuine typos. See hard_constraints.additional.did_you_mean_is_not_pure_edit_distance.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the "schedules" recipe (cron/schedule/scheduled aliases) need its own host.trigger.test-shaped third step, given host.trigger.test only supports message/webhook/event trigger kinds, not schedule?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: kinds::aliases::recipe_steps's "schedules" recipe uses host.trigger.fire (which fires any trigger by id regardless of kind) as its third step instead of host.trigger.test, so every recipe step names a call that actually works for that recipe's trigger kind, not just a registered tool name in the abstract (AC5 only requires the latter, but a recipe an agent can't actually run would defeat the PRD's own point).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should host.spec_test (handler.rs) gain alias resolution too, since it also looks up kind via KindRegistry::get?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- PRD requirements 2/3 name only host.quickstart and host.tool_publish; host.spec_test's own UnknownKind construction was updated only for the new `aliases` field (to keep the enum change compiling), not given resolve_kind's alias-lookup behavior. Out of scope per the coder dispatch's AC list.
